messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 542 omitted, sha256 a3a13a22116dc4e5>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The definition of Confidential Information is broad, covering all furnished information including business, financial, and operational data, not just technical information, so the hypothesis that it includes only technical information is false.
<quote check="exact">all analyses, compilations, data, studies, notes, interpretations, memoranda or other documents prepared by a party or its Representatives containing or based in whole or in part on any such furnished information are collectively referred to herein as the "Confidential Information;"</quote>
<quote check="exact">concerning its business prospects, financial condition, operations, assets and liabilities</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 96
reason: The Agreement defines Confidential Information broadly to cover business, financial, and operational information and derived analyses, not just technical information.
<quote check="exact">certain information concerning its business prospects, financial condition, operations, assets and liabilities</quote>
<quote check="exact">all such information furnished to a party or its Representatives (as defined below) by or on behalf of the other party (irrespective of the form of communication</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 90
reason: Confidential Information is defined broadly to cover business, financial, and operational information and all information furnished, not just technical information.
<quote check="exact">certain information concerning its business prospects, financial condition, operations, assets and liabilities</quote>
<quote check="exact">all such information furnished to a party or its Representatives (as defined below) by or on behalf of the other party (irrespective of the form of communication</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 93, "quotes": ["certain information concerning its business prospects, financial condition, operations, assets and liabilities", "all such information furnished to a party or its Representatives (as defined below) by or on behalf of the other party (irrespective of the form of communication"], "reason": "Confidential Information is defined as all information furnished by the other party, including business, financial and operational information, so it is not limited to technical information."}
